title: Connection fencing and epoch-based stream tombstones for graceful partial-generation cleanup
creator: Aisha Patel
description: When clients disconnect mid-generation (network blips, browser tab close, mobile sleep) we currently leak partial outputs and holding buffers on the server for up to the stream TTL. That increases memory pressure and complicates retry semantics for resumed sessions. This ticket implements a connection-fencing + epoch-based tombstone mechanism to: (1) enable prompt-safe reclamation of server resources for orphaned generations, (2) provide deterministic resume semantics for replay-capable clients, and (3) remain backward-compatible with older clients via a compatibility flag.
acceptance_criteria: Server creates an ‘epoch’ token for every streamed generation and associates it with the client connection; token is short-lived and monotonic per-client-connection
When a new connection is established for the same logical session, server fences previous epochs and creates tombstones marking partial state eligible for expedited GC
Tombstone TTLs are configurable per-customer and per-model; default expedited GC for ephemeral sessions reduces memory usage vs current TTL by >= 60% in benchmark scenario
Clients that support epoch resume can request a resume by providing last-seen epoch+offset; server validates and either rehydrates or rejects with a clear retryable error code
Older clients (no epoch header) continue to use existing TTL semantics and do not observe behavioral regressions
End-to-end tests covering disconnect -> reconnect -> resume flow, fencing, and tombstone GC are present in CI
design_decisions: Use monotonic 64-bit epoch per logical session (not per-connection) to avoid collisions when clients re-establish connections quickly
Tombstone objects are lightweight markers pointing to KV-cache snapshot id + token; actual payloads are reclaimed asynchronously to avoid blocking critical path
Expose epoch header via both REST and streaming websocket handshake; compatibility mode when header absent
Server-side fencing is authoritative: a new epoch implicitly marks older epochs as fenced and transitions their state to tombstone; fencing policy is idempotent
Avoid changing client-side backpressure units; server continues to use token-window and flow-control but adds epoch-awareness to avoid honoring stale inflight credits
implementation_notes: Add EpochManager component in runtime that maintains map<session_id, active_epoch, tombstone_meta>
Introduce tombstone_gc queue processed by background workers with per-customer rate-limit and memory budget checks
Add new header: X-Stream-Epoch and a handshake field in the streaming init frame: {epoch: <u64>, last_offset: <u32>}
Update streaming router to check epoch on each incoming frame; if frame epoch < active_epoch -> reject with 410 (Gone) + guidance header
Instrumentation: add metrics: epoch_rejected_total, tombstones_created_total, tombstone_gc_time_ms, orphaned_bytes_before_vs_after
Feature-flag rollout: initial opt-in beta for customers via console toggle, then gradual opt-out for those with compatibility issues
Memory benchmark scenario: 1000 concurrent ephemeral sessions, 1% disconnect rate per second; target reduce 95th percentile resident memory by >= 40%
progress_updates: 2026-03-02: Spike: implemented EpochManager prototype and handshake parsing in local runtime. Verified monotonic epoch assignment for new sessions.
2026-03-04: Integration test: established fencing behavior when new connection created; older epoch rejected as expected. Observed 15% memory improvement in micro-run (small sample).
2026-03-06: Design review with Runtime and Client SDK teams. Decision: keep header optional for backward compatibility; SDKs will auto-populate when available.
2026-03-08: Implemented tombstone GC worker with basic TTL; found pathological case where rehydration raced with GC - added rehydration lock and short grace window (200ms).
2026-03-10: Cross-team sync with Console owner: need per-customer config UI and API. Logged follow-up PM ticket PM-764 for console work.

2026-03-12: Load test: 1000 sessions, simulated disconnects. Memory 95p reduced 46% vs baseline; tombstone GC throughput ~800/s; identified edge-case where browser clients reconnected with older epoch due to network split—added explicit guidance code 410 and retry interval header
